chapter: Blackbirds, Carmen Jones and the Ziegfeld Follies
title: The Ziegfeld phone call and a $1,000-a-week offer
summary: A Ziegfeld caller reaches Buck at the stage door; Bubbles routes it to Nazarro, who arranges the audition at $500 each.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: However, after the show was over I would go down the street, we've got about three shows to make -- I go down the street to the corner, get some coffee in the meantime thinking over how this could have happened, Buck and Bubbles is up in lights. And from what I had said it would have no effect in my mind unless somebody was told, and who could I have told, I didn't tell anybody. And I had the coffee and the tears was rolling down my cheeks at the same time thinking this over, so I come back to the theater and when I come back to the theater -- the stage door is on the sidewalk, you go off the sidewalk to the stage door and

there's a vestibule inside and there's a phone on the wall at the end of the vestibule, right next to the staircase going back stage. And as I opened the door to go back stage, Buck was on the phone and saying to whoever was on the line, "Oh, here comes my partner now," with his hand over the mouthpiece, telling them, here comes my partner, just a moment. Then he puts his hand over the mouthpiece and says to me, "It's the Ziegfeld office calling." This is after the first show now. I says, "Really? Give it to me. I take the phone. I says, "Hello." "Mr. Ziegfeld wants to know when you can have an audition." Well, before we use any jokes we have to pass through the manager and the telephone number is Bryant 9-2335. Yeah, Nat Nazarro, yeah. "Okay. All right. Good-bye." I go upstairs and tell Buck, I don't know who it was but they got the gag, I give them the gag.
So after the next show, Nazarro's office called to say we just got a call from Ziegfeld. He wants you all to do an audition.

I said, 'Did you straighten it out?' Now he don't know I told him to call him. He doesn't know -- Nazarro don't know that I told the Ziegfeld office to call him. So he straightens it out for an audition and now he's already told us what a show it is, how many people want to go in it for nothing and we are now getting a salary of $1,000 a week. Understand?
For a whole act -- you and Buck $1,000 altogether?

However, we could go to Nazarro and get a hundred dollars any time. Just like Chuck comes to you to get something and in the future bookings you could let us have something that you had in mind or you get your money back, you always get your money back. So you have in mind that you're going to book so-and-so-and-so, he'd let us have the money. If he ain't got no money -- can't do it now,

got too many bills to pay and there ain't many people calling for your act now either, so you gotta wait till I get some offers or something. So I don't sanction him on that, I just sanction on the idea that I can get the money.
